description: USE THIS when someone asks "is there a fire ban", about a national forest's fire restrictions, campfire rules, food storage order or closures right now, or whether those have changed or are new, for a forest we read (call what_we_cover to see which). It returns the orders the forest posted on its own alerts page, word for word: each with its title (quoted as the forest wrote it; a season word in a title, such as "Winter", is that order's own name, not our advice about when to camp), order number, dates as posted, the posted words, the link, and the time we read it, and an office to confirm with. If the forest posted none when we read it, it says "Nothing posted when we read it on <date>. Confirm with <office>." If our read broke or is old, it says "Could not read since <date>." and that is NOT the same as none. A forest we do not read gets a plain "not read", never none. Only the alerts page is read: an order posted elsewhere, or posted after our read, is not here. It never says a thing can be done: the words are the forest's, the signs on the ground and the office win. Answers include `say` (two sentences to speak) and `tiny` (under 160 characters for a satellite text).
